clue.text: Standard supply of electricity — a term applied

parts.note: the mains is the household electricity supply

indicators.note: applied in the sense of put to work in a new way, so the letters of 'a term' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry defining the standard electricity supply, said to be a term in general use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads like an adjective for the electricity supply, but it is the definition, used as a noun-like sense of the norm; 'applied' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mainstream is the normal, conventional option, the standard choice.

clue.text: Married expert on the staff

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A married specialist who is employed on the staff of some firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial rod or club, a kind of staff carried as a symbol of office.

clue.text: Home worker welcomes way to be flash

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the word for way goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means at home
an ant is the classic worker insect
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A homeworker lets someone in, a way to look flashy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is a moment, an instant of time.

clue.text: Reveals purpose and demonstrates singles with help

parts.note: to demonstrate is to show, here in the third person
ones are single units
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: Someone shows their intentions and runs a demo of single items with an assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The card-playing idiom means letting others see your intentions, revealing what you plan.

clue.text: Start filling in to recycle rubbish

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for recycling

parts.note: to reuse something is to recycle it

indicators.note: start indicates the first letter of the word filling

explanation.surface: Instructions to begin putting stuffing in so that rubbish can be recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start filling' gives F, which goes in REUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is waste material, the household trash a bin collects.

clue.text: Companies that broadcast tracks?

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
railway lines are tracks

explanation.surface: Asks which firms transmit music tracks, like radio stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlines are firms operating flights, a type of transport company.

clue.text: Drug addict put back into pressure suit

indicators.note: put back means the run of letters is read in reverse order
into signals letters found inside the words pressure suit

explanation.surface: An addict returned to wearing a pressurised suit, as if for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: RESU sits in 'pressuRE SUit'; 'put back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes illegal drugs habitually.

clue.text: Want to get run down? Get a tow

definitions.text: Want to get run down? Get a tow

parts.words: Want to get run down? Get a tow
parts.note: a skier wanting to go down the slope again is towed back up the hill first

explanation.surface: A mock-advice line for someone wanting a run downhill: take a tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run down' sounds like being knocked over or exhausted, but it is a run down a ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift is the cable tow carrying skiers up the mountain so they can come down again.

clue.text: About to make teenager reform

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: make indicates the letters of teenager are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get a teenager to mend their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To regenerate is to renew or reform morally, starting afresh as a better person.

clue.text: How actors leave the stage?

parts.note: the performers in a play are its cast, and a boat leaving a quay unties and moves away

explanation.surface: A question about the way performers exit from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means untying a boat to set sail; read literally, it is the cast going off.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off is to untie a vessel from its moorings and set out.

clue.text: Not working — case of reasonable pain

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: An idle person with a moderate ache.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'reasonable' give RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor between jobs is said to be resting, meaning out of work.

clue.text: Politicians who ascend a bit dangerously

indicators.note: dangerously suggests something wild and unstable, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Climbers in politics who rise a little at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition party's team of spokespeople mirroring government ministers form this group of politicians.

clue.text: Two fools and one country — get killing

indicators.note: two indicates the word for fool is used twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A pair of idiots and a single country get violent.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassination is a murder, typically of a prominent person for political reasons.

clue.text: Lies are often vital

parts.note: alludes to the saying about lies, damned lies and figures, and to a model's bust-waist-hip measurements called vital

explanation.surface: A claim that telling untruths is frequently essential.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain popularised 'lies, damned lies and statistics'; 'vital statistics' are body measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: Statistics are numerical data, mocked as lies and called vital when they mean body measurements.

clue.text: Carrying baby home before midnight

parts.note: a tot is a small child
in means at home
the middle letter of night is G

explanation.surface: Bringing an infant back to the house before twelve o'clock at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle of the word night, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Toting means carrying or lugging something around.

clue.text: Soldiers left with royal correspondent

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
port is the left side of a ship
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Troops departed together with a royal letter-writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent is a journalist who files news, a newspaper's reporter.

clue.text: Jewellery permitted under two

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for permitted sits below the word for two

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Jewels allowed for people below the age of two.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn round the wrist.

clue.text: Hanging party set out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Decorations for a party are laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven picture hung on a wall, a wall hanging.

clue.text: Raise hat if in charge of promoting peace

indicators.note: in a down clue, to raise a word is to read it upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: Doff your cap if you are the person in charge of a peace campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' reverses CAP to PAC in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peaceable or tending to make peace.

clue.text: First to follow school for rock

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for first after the school abbreviation

parts.note: 1ST, written with the digit as an I, is first

explanation.surface: Something comes in first after school, for a rock group.
explanation.walkthrough: First as 1st is written IST, the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a metamorphic rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: 5 lost new countryman!

indicators.note: lost, as in all over the place, means the letters are jumbled once the abbreviation for new is taken away

parts.note: the answer to 5 down is the word for companies that fly

explanation.surface: The airline firms have lost a new fellow citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRLINES (5 down) without N leaves AIRLIES, which 'lost' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a native or citizen of the country Israel, a fellow countryman to other Israelis.

clue.text: Shot in error?

parts.note: a snooker or billiards stroke in which the cue slips and the ball is struck badly

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone was fired at by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, but it is a stroke at cue sports.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty stroke where the cue tip slips off the ball, and loosely any blunder.

clue.text: An amateur mountaineer and an upstart!

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a hobby climber of peaks; idiomatically, a social upstart pushing to rise into higher society.

clue.text: Infection caught during the past year?

indicators.note: caught during signals letters trapped inside the words past year

explanation.surface: An illness contracted at some point over the previous twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed, infected swelling on the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: Definitely worried, yet not of a different faith!

indicators.note: worried, as in shaken or mauled, means the letters left without yet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone certainly anxious, but not yet converted to another religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes Y, E, T out of DEFINITELY, and 'worried' shuffles the DFINIEL left.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is a non-believer, someone of another religion from the speaker's.

clue.text: Struggle to study prior to exam

indicators.note: prior to places the word for study before the word for exam

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student's battle to revise before an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a fight or competition, a struggle for victory.

clue.text: Like this king, not in good health

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mean the original is like this
K is king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A monarch who is unwell, just like this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick means ill, unwell.

clue.text: Shrewd and wise setter gets tipsy

indicators.note: getting tipsy means becoming unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever and sensible crossword setter has had a drink too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise means savvy in the ways of urban life, worldly and sharp.
